hits.snippet:
While the European Commission is attempting to deregulate new genome modification techniques (NGT), the US company Pairwise is multiplying its “*partnerships*” combining the Crispr/Cas tool and its Fulcrum platform.
...
In November 2025, Pairwise signed a licensing agreement with the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) to allow the institute to use its patented CRISPR/Cas tool.
This agreement is one of many^1^ concerning the Crispr tool, for which Pairwise itself holds an exclusive licence from Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) for the development of agricultural applications^2^.
Through its Fulcrum platform, using its own Crispr SHARC enzyme, Pairwise claims to be “*developing new traits quickly without creating GMOs*“.
...
Pairwise was co-founded in March 2017 by Tom Adams, a former Monsanto executive, Feng Zengh of the Broad Institute, one of the first researchers to work on Crispr, and other scientists (from Harvard Medical School, MGH, etc.) with the aim of developing the use of Crispr in agriculture.
...
In April 2020, Pairwise established its first partnership with Plant Sciences to create various GMO berries, including black raspberries, “*which naturally have five times more antioxidants than blueberries… and, when genetically modified, expand growing seasons and enable year-round production*“.
In May 2023, the company launched its Fulcrum platform*, * which it describes as *“using Pairwise developed genetic editing tools, artificial intelligence and a library of traits and expertise*“.
Through this platform, Pairwise licenses Crispr patent rights, which it owns or controls, to multinationals such as Corteva and Bayer.
...
Pairwise is continuing this approach, announcing in June 2024 that it has developed the first seedless blackberry *via * its Fulcrum platform.
...
In September 2025, Pairwise confirmed this by announcing a “*strategic partnership with Sun World International to develop the Holy Grail of fruits and vegetables: the pitless cherry*.”
In mid-November 2025, it granted a new licence for its Fulcrum platform to the Dutch company Enza Zaden for the development of “*novel* * crop varieties and sustainable farming practices”.
...
It holds a significant patent position on CRISPR, grants licences to private and public partners, and is thus positioning itself as a technology platform that may become difficult to circumvent.

hits.title: Seedless blackberry developed through gene editing
hits.snippet:
Monday, October 19, 2026
...
June 05, 2024
Pairwise, a company pioneering genetics-based innovation in food and agriculture, has developed the world’s first seedless blackberry.
Created using the company’s proprietrary Fulcrum Platform, a complete suite of novel tools for CRISPR application in plants, this is the first time seedlessness has been achieved in any caneberry.
“We are thrilled to share this breakthrough achievement from our talented R&D team.
Pairwise scientists have used their deep knowledge of plant genetics, broad suite of CRISPR tools, and multiplex editing techniques to eliminate the hard pits in berry fruit, creating soft, small seeds like those found in grapes and watermelon that are commonly labeled as seedless,” said Ryan Bartlett, Pairwise chief technology officer.
“The result is the first seedless blackberry in the world.
We expect that this trait will not only transform the blackberry market, but it also lays the groundwork for accelerated progress in removing seeds and pits in many other fruits such as cherries.”
“The berry variety we edited is consistently sweet year-round and holds up well during shipment; now, consumers will have the option to choose a nutritious blackberry without seeds that also reliably delivers great flavour and quality,” said Haven Baker, Pairwise co-founder and chief business officer.
...
In addition to creating the first seedless caneberry, Pairwise has successfully edited the same variety to eliminate thorns and create a more compact plant that delivers benefits for harvesters, growers, and the environment.
Early data from Pairwise-led trials indicate the potential to greatly increase yield per acre while necessitating only a minimal increase in inputs – meaning the water and land used per crate of fruit harvested decreases significantly.

This is the power of modern genomics, introducing speed, precision, and the ability to solve multiple problems to the glacially slow, haphazard, one-tweak-at-a-time world of crop breeding.** ** Pairwise’s triple-threat berries won’t be in US groceries before 2030—even turbo-charged breeding takes time—but they could help jump-start a new agricultural revolution, a high-tech era of designer crops optimized to benefit consumers, farmers, and the Earth.

# Investigative report — Pairwise, Fulcrum and edited berries

**Cut-off:** 20 October 2026, inclusive.  
**Bottom line:** Pairwise has **demonstrated CRISPR-edited seedless/soft-seed, prickleless and compact blackberry traits**, field-tested blackberry material in the United States and Colombia, and commercially sold **limited quantities of the compact/high-density blackberry in Colombia**. The newly named **Fontana™** is the compact commercial product; Pairwise’s own 14 October announcement does **not** call Fontana seedless or thornless, instead placing those traits in later pipeline varieties. The seedless blackberry remained in field testing and was not established as commercially available anywhere by the cut-off. [257][196][375]

## 1. Identity, domains, aliases, parents and subsidiaries

| Entity / aliases | Official domain and legal identity | Parent, subsidiaries or affiliates established in this pass | HQ versus program geography | Evidence, date and short exact excerpt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pairwise; Pairwise Plants; Pairwise Plants Services** | Official domain: **https://www.pairwise.com/**. Public legal documents use both **Pairwise Plants, LLC**, a Delaware LLC, and **Pairwise Plants Services, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation. Pairwise’s privacy notice says the website is operated by “Pairwise Plants Services and its affiliates” but gives the postal addressee as Pairwise Plants, LLC. [76][420] | The precise ownership chain between the LLC and Services Inc. is **not established in this research pass**. No wholly owned operating subsidiary was affirmatively identified. Pairwise is privately held; Deerfield, Leaps by Bayer, Aliment, Temasek and Corteva are investors, not parents. | HQ: 807 E. Main Street, Durham, NC; additional RTP site: 110 TW Alexander Drive, Durham. Blackberry field trials: US and Colombia; limited commercial fruit sales: Colombia. These are program locations, not headquarters. [78][196] | Pairwise, About, current: “**founded in 2017** by CEO Tom Adams… Haven Baker… Feng Zhang… David Liu… and J. Keith Joung.” [77] Privacy policy, effective 1 Jan 2023: “**Pairwise Plants Services and its affiliates**.” [76] |
| **Plant Sciences, Inc.; PSI** | Legacy official domain reported as **https://plantsciences.com/**; address 342 Green Valley Road, Watsonville, California. [68][69] | PSI and its affiliated breeding interests created **Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc. (PSG)**. PSI remained the contracted research-and-propagation service provider. It was not shown to be owned by Simplot or Pairwise. | HQ/operations: Watsonville, California; nurseries in the US and Mexico and master-license relationships in Europe; genetics supplied in 50+ countries. [438] | 1 Aug 2023 restructuring: “**PSI will serve PSG, under contract, providing research and propagation services**.” [67] |
| **Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc.; PSG; Plant Sciences Genetics®** | Official domain: **https://www.plantsciencesgenetics.com/**. California nursery records name **Plant Sciences Genetics, Incorporated**. [61][72] | PSG received berry populations and IP previously held by **Plant Sciences, Berry Genetics, Strawberry Sciences, Via Berry Breeding, Vitae Caneberry Breeding and Fragaria Plant Sciences**. Whether every predecessor was dissolved, retained as an affiliate or merely transferred assets is **not established**. [435] | Watsonville, California; testing and licensing are global. | PSG history: “**In 2024, Plant Sciences consolidated its breeding program… under the new name, Plant Sciences Genetics**.” [61] The 2023 release says PSG would hold 15 populations: 8 strawberry, 3 blueberry, 2 raspberry, 1 blackberry and 1 black raspberry. [67] |
| **J.R. Simplot Company; Simplot; Simplot Plant Sciences** | Official corporate domain: **https://www.simplot.com/**. | A privately held Simplot company; no ownership of PSI/PSG established. “Simplot Plant Sciences” appears as the submitting unit on USDA documents, not evidence that PSI is its subsidiary. | Boise, Idaho corporate base; strawberry germplasm and growing expertise came from Watsonville-based PSI; planned market work included US and Canada. | Simplot, 28 Oct 2021: “**strategic alliance with Plant Sciences Inc. … including gene editing**”; Simplot supplies editing technology, PSI germplasm, growing expertise and commercialization leadership. [166] |
| **Plantik Biosciences; Plantik** | Official domain: **https://www.plantik.bio/**. French legal entity **PLANTIK BIOSCIENCES**, company no. 853088441, organized as an SAS. [334] | Parent or subsidiaries: **not established**. Founded by Ying Shao and Aditya Nayak. | Registered/operating references point to France: Paris/Station F and an R&D presence in the Genopole cluster at Évry-Courcouronnes. Tomato demonstrations occurred in the US and Belgium; strawberry work is with Dutch HRB. [331][333][336] | Genopole describes Plantik as accelerating “**the conventional plant breeding process**,” but its actual ATLANTIS programs select non-coding targets subsequently genome-edited; “advanced breeding” language should not be read as absence of editing. [133][336] |
| **Hudson River Biotechnology B.V.; Hudson River; HRB** | Official domain: **https://www.hudsonriver.bio/**. Dutch legal name: **Hudson River Biotechnology B.V.** [350] | No parent or subsidiaries established. Investors include Bridford Group, Oost NL and Spanish agro-innovation investor Eurogenetic/Eurosemillas; these are not shown as parents. [345][346] | Wageningen, Netherlands. Programs/services cover tomatoes, strawberries, vegetables, soft fruit and other species. | HRB platform page: “**DNA-free method of CRISPR, called Protoplasting**.” [351] Pairwise agreement dated 26 May 2026 gave HRB access to Fulcrum for editing services. [91] |
| **Fall Creek Farm & Nursery, Inc.; Fall Creek®; Sekoya®** | Official domain: **https://www.fallcreeknursery.com/**. Legal operating name used publicly: Fall Creek Farm & Nursery, Inc. | Family-owned; ten wholly owned operating units are reported, but their complete legal names were **not established**. **Sekoya is a commercial blueberry platform, not established as a separate corporate parent.** | Founded and headquartered in Oregon; facilities across North/South America, Europe, Asia and Africa; genetics in 59–65+ countries. [321][327] | Fall Creek describes two routes: **Fall Creek Collection** and coordinated licensed platform **Sekoya**. [321] No Pairwise/Fulcrum or berry-editing relationship was established. |
| **Planasa; Plantas de Navarra, S.A.; Planasa Group** | Official domain: **https://planasa.com/**. Website owner is **Plantas de Navarra, S.A.**, NIF A31039795. The consolidation parent historically identified in policies is **Tigruti ITG, S.L.U.** [414][406] | Acquired by Germany’s **EW Group** in 2024 according to Planasa’s sustainability report; Planasa subsequently acquired Illinois Foundation Seeds in 2026. Group entities include Planasa Viveros and international operating companies, but a complete current subsidiary schedule was **not established**. [405][318] | Valtierra, Navarra, Spain; breeding/nursery sites in Europe, the Americas and Africa. The March 2026 Planasa/Fall Creek events occurred at Cartaya and Aznalcázar, Spain, not their global HQs. [328] | Legal notice: “**owner… is Plantas de Navarra, S.A., hereinafter PLANASA**.” [414] No Pairwise/Fulcrum relationship was established. |
| **Ohalo Genetics; Boosted Breeding™** | Official domain: **https://www.ohalo.com/**. Included only to resolve the terminology. | No corporate connection to Pairwise, PSG, Simplot, Plantik, HRB, Fall Creek or Planasa was established. | Ohalo reports work across potatoes, corn, berries and other crops. | Ohalo, 17/23 May 2024: “**Boosted Breeding™**” is Ohalo’s branded system. [122][123] **It must not be treated as a synonym for CRISPR, Fulcrum, or generic advanced breeding.** |

### Identity conclusion

- **PSI and PSG are related but not interchangeable.** PSI was the 2020 contracting party and germplasm/nursery partner; PSG later became the holder/marketer of the consolidated berry populations and associated IP. [151][435]
- **Pairwise is not shown to own PSI/PSG**, and PSI/PSG is not shown to own Pairwise.
- **Simplot’s PSI alliance is separate from Pairwise’s PSI caneberry alliance.**
- **Fall Creek and Planasa merely coordinated 2026 industry events.** That is not evidence of a joint breeding company, IP license or gene-editing program. The announcement explicitly says each retained ownership of its event. [317]
- **No Chinese company was identified as a named berry partner in the investigated network.** Pairwise reports undisclosed Fulcrum licenses in China for grains and legumes, but not a Chinese berry licensee; therefore no Chinese company name can responsibly be supplied here in Chinese. [300]

## 2. Blackberry lineage, products, traits and stage

| Product / material | Base genetics and responsible parties | Technology and demonstrated traits | Status by 20 Oct 2026 | Exact supporting evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PSG BK-613 / Rejoice / PS-BK3-17.006-13** | Conventionally bred PSI/PSG primocane blackberry. Public sources connect BK-613 with the cultivar shown by PSG as **Rejoice**, legal cultivar denomination **PS-BK3-17.006-13**, protected by US Plant Patent PP34,597. [390][400][402] | Conventional breeding parent/background; high yield, low drupelet reversion, firmness/postharvest and flavor. No evidence the original PSG cultivar was edited. | Commercial/scaling PSG cultivar; reported expectation of 1,000+ North American acres by March 2025. Independent confirmation of achieved acreage was not established. | PSG page: “**Rejoice – The New Standard of Blackberry / PS-BK3-17.006-13**.” [402] |
| **Pairwise seedless or soft-seed prototype** | Pairwise edited a proprietary PSG/PSI eastern tetraploid blackberry. Secondary reporting identifies BK-613 as the base, but Pairwise’s launch release only says the same proprietary variety and later Fontana material is “built on a proven PSG variety.” Exact lineage equivalence is therefore **probable but not conclusively disclosed by Pairwise**. [392][375] | Fulcrum CRISPR with multiplex edits targeting seed-pit/endocarp development. Result is not literally seed-free: “**soft, small seeds like those found in grapes and watermelon that are commonly labeled as seedless**.” Pairwise separately edited the same variety for pricklessness and compact architecture. [257] | Announced/demonstrated in greenhouse June 2024; outdoor field trials during 2025–26; not commercially available by the cut-off. [257][33] | Pairwise, 4 Jun 2024: “**first time seedlessness has been achieved in any caneberry**” and availability expected “in a few years.” [5] |
| **Edited compact/high-density blackberry sold in Colombia** | Pairwise product on PSG germplasm; production partner and retailers were not named. | CRISPR-edited compact architecture; higher planting density, shorter production cycle and higher prospective yield. Public evidence conflicts on whether the Colombia lots also had thornless/soft-seed edits. Pairwise’s clearest 2025 field-trial statement says compact blackberries were “paving the way” for future seedless berries, so the conservative conclusion is **compact only unless the lot-level genotype is disclosed**. [208] | First Colombian field trial announced 29 May 2025; small-scale/limited commercial fruit sales followed in late 2025 and were reported by Pairwise in Jan 2026. Demonstrated commercial sale, not broad retail launch. [196][203] | Pairwise, Jan 2026: “**first commercial sale of edited blackberries in the world… In Colombia… sold to consumers**.” [196] Retailers, volume, price and producer were not disclosed. [201] |
| **Fontana™** | Pairwise product “built on a proven PSG variety.” Likely the named commercial continuation of the compact Colombian program, but the announcement does not expressly equate every Colombian lot with Fontana or publicly name BK-613/Rejoice as its base. | Compact primocane: 3.5–5 ft; higher density; no pruning; minimal trellis labor; 109–125 days to harvest; 7,500–10,500 clamshells per acre per cycle and “up to” 18,000/year, according to Pairwise. Fruit 8–10 g, low color reversion and high firmness. These remain company performance claims; footnotes and independent replicated trial data were absent from the page. [46] | Named/introduced 14 Oct 2026 “for commercial fresh-market production.” Colombia had limited commercial compact-fruit sales, but plant ordering, licensees, prices and country-by-country Fontana availability were not published. It is **not established as broadly commercially available**. | Pairwise: “**Fontana is the first in a pipeline… which include thornless and seedless blackberries**.” Thus Fontana itself was not represented as seedless or thornless. [375] |
| **Future thornless blackberry** | Pairwise/PSG pipeline. | CRISPR loss of function in **RuWOX1** has been scientifically demonstrated to eliminate prickles in an elite tetraploid commercial blackberry line. | Demonstrated in plants; future named commercial variety not established. | *Plant Physiology*, 2026: independent loss-of-function mutations in **WOX1** underlie the prickleless S locus; all edited plants were prickleless, with no other observed morphological difference. [478][479] |
| **Black and red raspberry programs** | Pairwise + PSI/PSG, drawing on public/private Rubus diversity work. | Announced targets included taste, convenience, shelf life and off-season availability; USDA exemptions include edited black raspberry traits. | Research, trait validation and regulatory exemptions demonstrated; a named commercial Pairwise raspberry product was **not established**. | Pairwise–PSI, 15 Apr 2020: teams would focus on “**black and red raspberries, as well as blackberries**.” [151] |

## 3. Editing versus conventional or “advanced” breeding

| Company/program | What is conventional | What is actually gene edited | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PSI/PSG** | Core germplasm and cultivars, including the background blackberry, are produced through crossing, selection and other breeding technologies. PSG explicitly offers “traditional crossing techniques.” [63] | Caneberry editing is supplied through Pairwise; strawberry editing through Simplot. PSG’s site says Pairwise editing is being implemented “across our caneberry breeding programs,” while Simplot applies it in strawberry programs. [436] | Do not describe all PSG varieties as edited. The edited trait is layered onto conventionally bred elite germplasm. |
| **Pairwise/Fulcrum** | Pairwise sometimes says its edits are “achievable by conventional breeding,” reflecting the wording of a US regulatory exemption—not that the plants were conventionally bred. [181] | Fulcrum integrates CRISPR cutting, base editing, templated editing, AI and trait libraries. SHARC is Pairwise’s proprietary CRISPR enzyme; REDRAW is its RNA-templated DNA replacement tool.
